bounded_statement: Within the supplied files for case:ae33434a6064f4251cbc, the selected result (two-sample Student t-test of ctmax_c by shore zone, t(46) = -30.402, p < 0.0001, n = 24 per group) was computed by entering all four repeated ramp-day measurements of each of the 12 limpets as separate independent observations in a row-independent two-sample t-test, even though the data description designates limpet_id as the independent unit (6 animals per zone). The reported sample sizes (24 per group) and degrees of freedom (46) therefore reflect measurement rows rather than independent animals, so the stated test statistic and p-value are not supported as reported; a unit-correct analysis would have 6 observations per group (df = 10).

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the repeated-measures structure (6 animals per zone, 4 ramps per animal), so the row-level entry is not concealed; and the between-zone gap (2.400 C) is large relative to within- and between-animal variation, so a unit-correct per-animal analysis (6 vs 6 animal means) would very likely still find a significant difference. This mitigates the practical impact on the direction of the conclusion but does not make the reported t(46), p-value, or n = 24 per group valid as stated.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: Animals = 6 per zone disclosed; difference 2.400 C with SD 0.273 C

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the finding by checking (1) whether the workflow aggregates to one value per limpet before testing: split_by_zone appends ctmax_c for every row and only deduplicates the animal tag list for counting, so no aggregation occurs; (2) whether the reported statistics could correspond to a unit-level test: the reported n = 24 per group and df = 46 = 48 - 2 exactly match row-level entry, not the 6-per-group, df = 10 test that per-animal analysis would give; (3) whether the shore_zone factor might vary within a limpet, making rows the appropriate unit: in the data each limpet_id has a single fixed shore_zone across its four rows, so the treatment is applied at the animal level and the animal is the correct analysis unit, consistent with the description's designated independent-unit column. All three checks confirm rather than refute the issue.

root_cause: The workflow's split_by_zone function appends every row's ctmax_c value to the zone's value list without aggregating by limpet_id, and build_report passes these full 24-row-per-zone lists directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind. Because each limpet contributes four highly similar repeated readings, the t-test's independence assumption is violated: the effective sample is 6 animals per zone, not 24 measurements, inflating n and degrees of freedom (46 instead of 10) and overstating the precision of the reported statistic.
